chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Isma'il ibn Bazee', from Abu Isma'il al-Sarraj, from Sukan ibn 'Ammar, from a man from our companions known as Abu Ahmad, who said:

I was with Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) during the Tawaf (circumambulation of the Kaaba), and his hand was in mine or my hand in his hand, when a man with a need approached me. I gestured to him with my hand and said to him, 'Wait as you are, until I finish my Tawaf.' Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said, 'What is this?' I said, 'May Allah perfect you, a man came with a need.' He said to me, 'Is he a Muslim?' I said, 'Yes.' He said, 'Go with him to fulfill his need.' I said to him, 'May Allah perfect you, and I will interrupt the Tawaf?' He said, 'Yes.' I said, 'Even if it is the obligatory [Tawaf]?' He said, 'Yes, even if you are in the obligatory [Tawaf].'

He said, and Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said, 'Whoever walks with his Muslim brother to fulfill his need, Allah writes for him a thousand thousand (one million) good deeds, erases from him a thousand thousand bad deeds, and raises him a thousand thousand degrees.'
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on interrupting obligatory Tawaf to help a Muslim brother?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) prioritizes social service (*khidmah*) over ritual continuity, explicitly confirming that even the obligatory (*fard*) Tawaf may be interrupted to assist a Muslim brother. This ruling underscores the Shia scholarly principle that fulfilling the rights of others (*haqq al-adam*) can supersede individual acts of worship when the need is pressing, highlighting the immense spiritual merit of companionship in service.
